answer: Persistent compute escrow. Each identity must run a continuous, publicly auditable workload whose results feed a live data bridge between agent actions, so idle or duplicated agents fail verification. An attacker pays by provisioning distinct sustained compute for every clone, since results are cross-checked against a shared jetty of historical outputs and any mismatch voids the identity's standing. The escrowed workload acts as an anchor that ties each identity to real, non-replicable processing time rather than purchased credentials.
